checkpoints.description: [1/4] Clear endpoint safety: only POST/DELETE clear, all other methods 405, drain request body

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed HEAD /__clear wipes the inbox, defeating the documented prefetch protection, and POST /__clear with a body aborts the client with WinError 10053.
impact_assessment.benefits: Read-only probes can no longer destroy captures, and clients sending a body get a stable response.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: HEAD/OPTIONS/CONNECT/TRACE on clear change from destructive to 405, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: an oversized body is drained only up to a bound.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use an explicit allowed-method set, drain a bounded prefix before answering, and add raw-socket failing-first tests for every method plus a body-bearing POST.

checkpoints.head: cb4c10f40e9fe071ffa19837b779d9be1c9e9678

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Reject truncated request bodies instead of storing partial payloads

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a client declaring 100 bytes but sending 3 gets 200 and a truncated body stored as if complete, corrupting any later replay or analysis.
impact_assessment.benefits: Captures are guaranteed to match the declared body length; incomplete webhooks are refused loudly.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: malformed clients now get 400 instead of 200; dependency: none; concurrency: check occurs before the store write; state: no partial record can be persisted.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Compare received bytes with Content-Length before constructing the record, add a raw-socket failing-first test, and document the response in README and ADR-012.

checkpoints.head: ff2bb51f90a0f4bb5683ce5adbddbb9f77c47ceb

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Reject malformed received_at values at record construction

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a bad timestamp is stored and imported, then one such record makes every time-filtered list fail with a misleading generic error.
impact_assessment.benefits: Inbox records always carry parseable timestamps, so time filtering cannot be broken by a single bad capture or snapshot.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: snapshots or records with invalid timestamps are now refused, so README and ADR must follow; dependency: stdlib datetime only; concurrency: none; state: validation occurs before any write.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Parse in __post_init__ with a Z-tolerant fromisoformat, raise CorruptInboxError, and add failing-first tests for construction and import.

checkpoints.head: b77e53e52b0e20b83237f4e5030f9e828c4d7c39

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Ignore OS-level client disconnects when writing HTTP responses

impact_assessment.why: A probe showed a normal client disconnect before reading the response produces a full ConnectionAbortedError traceback while the capture itself succeeds.
impact_assessment.benefits: Clean operator console; no confusing stack traces for routine disconnects.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, the HTTP status is unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: per-thread write path only; state: capture is persisted before the response is written.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Catch OSError around wfile.write with a documented hygiene allowance, and use a mocked wfile failing-first test.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Done: response writes tolerate client disconnect; 80 tests green
